target.title: fix(security): confine include permission remediation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where running `openclaw security audit --fix` could tighten permissions on a file outside the configured include roots when an invalid `$include` path referenced it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The permission scanner now uses the same guarded include resolver as config loading, so it only reports files that passed root containment, symlink, regular-file, and size checks. The supplied environment is preserved so configured include roots remain eligible for auditing.

## User Impact

Operators can run the security fixer without it changing permissions on escaped include targets. Legitimate files from `OPENCLAW_INCLUDE_ROOTS` continue to be checked and remediated.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/includes.test.ts src/security/fix.test.ts` — 2 files / 67 tests passed.
- Direct runtime probe: an escaped `../victim.json5` include remained mode `0644` and produced no include permission action.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/config/includes-scan.ts src/config/includes.test.ts src/security/fix.ts src/security/audit-extra.async.ts src/security/fix.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine codex --thinking high` — clean after the environment propagation fix.
- Remote Testbox proof is currently blocked because this environment is not authenticated to the `openclaw` Blacksmith organization; CI is required for the pushed head.

AI-assisted: built with Codex.
